2012_040_090412regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of September 4, 2012, at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. It recognizes 16 spring 2012 all-state athletes and a twenty-third consecutive ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting, and carries consent-agenda minutes from July 17 and August 14, 2012, twenty new teacher contracts, and reports on staffing, summer learning, enrollment, and the Superintendent's Annual Report. The principal action item is Bid Award #9745 for Adobe licenses to Logisoft Computer Products LLC at $31,266.40 per year for a three-year term totaling $93,799.20.
2012_040_090412regmtg.page:
**Meeting**

Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, September 4, 2012, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. (except July and August) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**

Mr. Jolly read biographies of 16 spring 2012 all-state athletes: Elizabeth Abro, Dakota Badder, Haley Burns, Kalie Collins, Jay Darish, Thomas Eng, Matthew Fitzpatrick, Madison Hirsch, Alison Holland, Oliver Jiang, Nick Kondoleon, Kamryn LaCarter, Antonina Malyarenko, Sinclair Russell, Rachel Sacco, and Irene Young, across girls soccer, boys and girls lacrosse, girls tennis, baseball, softball, and girls track.

For the twenty-third year in a row the district earned the ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting, for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2011. The June 13, 2012, award letter from Executive Director John D. Musso was addressed to Finance Director Monica Papasian; the certificate is also signed by President Brian L. Mee. Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, was recognized.

**Consent agenda**

Minutes of the July 17, 2012, special meeting (resolutions 12-078 appointing Jonathan Cross Assistant Principal of Baker Middle School effective July 18, 2012, and 12-079 approving new hires); minutes of the August 14, 2012, regular meeting (resolutions 12-080 through 12-085); and Bid Award #9745 for Adobe software.

**Bid Award #9745 - Adobe licenses**

Bids opened August 16, 2012; sent to five bidders, five received, none a no bid, two disqualified for not meeting specifications.

| Vendor | Unit cost | Annual cost | 3-year term |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDW Government LLC | $54.24 | $32,815.20 | $98,445.60 |
| Computer Intelligence Association | $52.22 | $31,593.10 | $94,779.93 |
| Logisoft Computer Products LLC | $51.86 | $31,266.40 | $93,799.20 |

Award recommended to Logisoft, charged to the General Fund technology budget through fiscal year 2014-15.

**Personnel**

Probationary contracts recommended for twenty teachers for 2012-2013, including Kristen Barry (First Grade, Costello), Ransom Brown (1.0 FTE Physics, Troy High), Sharon Douglas-Chong (1.0 FTE Mathematics, Troy High), Michael Millman (1.0 FTE EI Classroom, Martell), Suzanne Powell (1.0 FTE Counselor, Baker/Larson), and Caitlin Wettlaufer (Visual Art). Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources Jasen Witt reported 46 new TSD teachers, 9 previously tenured in another Michigan district, and 21 with a minimum of a master's degree, attributing hiring to MPSERS-driven retirements and resignations, the move to full-day kindergarten for 2012/2013, full-year leaves, FTE reductions, and increased enrollment at some buildings. Under new Board Policy #G-1006 Teacher Placement (adopted June 2012), the union raised 5 involuntary-transfer instances (1 elementary, 4 secondary).

A resolution proposed rescheduling the November 6, 2012, board meeting to November 13, 2012, at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building.
2012_040_090412regmtg.verbose:
**Meeting and format.** Cover and agenda for the regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education on September 4, 2012, at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district address 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000, web site www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The eleven-item agenda covers Pledge of Allegiance, Recognition, Additions and Deletions, Public Communication, a General consent agenda, Personnel, Curriculum, Business, Public Communication for non-agenda items, Other, and Adjournment.

**Recognition A - All-State Athletes, Spring 2012.** Mr. Jolly read biographies for sixteen athletes: Elizabeth Abro (Junior, Athens High School, girls soccer, coach Todd Heugh); Dakota Badder (Senior, Athens, boys lacrosse, coach Nick Stensen); Haley Burns (Senior, Troy High School, girls lacrosse, coach Allison Atchoo); Kalie Collins (Senior, Troy High, girls tennis, coach Brian Miska); Jay Darish (Sophomore, Troy High, boys lacrosse, coach Towbey Kassa); Thomas Eng (Senior, Athens, baseball, coach Mike Morris); Matthew Fitzpatrick (Senior, Athens, boys lacrosse); Madison Hirsch and Alison Holland (Juniors, Troy High, girls soccer, coach Brian Zawislak); Oliver Jiang and Nick Kondoleon (Seniors, Troy High, boys lacrosse); Kamryn LaCarter (Senior, Troy High, softball, coach Tom Calnen); Antonina Malyarenko (Senior, Troy High, girls tennis); Sinclair Russell (Senior, Athens, girls track, coach Mike Stallsmith); Rachel Sacco (Junior, Troy High, girls lacrosse); and Irene Young (Senior, Troy High, girls soccer, All State, All League, All District, All Area, All Region and Dream Team in 2012 and 2011, and Miss Soccer 2012). Honors cited include All State first, second and third team placements and All League, All District and All Region selections.

**Recognition B - ASBO award.** For the twenty-third year in a row the Troy School District earned the Association of School Business Officials International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for its Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2011. A June 13, 2012, letter from Executive Director John D. Musso, CAE, RSBA, to Finance Director Monica Papasian at 4400 Livernois conveys the award, notes review-panel comments to use in preparing the fiscal year end 2012 CAFR, encloses a sample press release, and advises that the engraved plaque and certificate would be mailed in approximately 6-8 weeks. The certificate is signed by President Brian L. Mee, SFO, RSBA, and by Musso. Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and his staff were recognized at the podium.

**Consent agenda item A - minutes of July 17, 2012 special meeting.** Vice-President Edmunds called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m. in the Administration Building; also present were Board members Hauff, Miletti and Underwood, administrators Machesky and Witt, and approximately 4 members of the audience. Resolution 12-078, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Ms. Underwood, issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Jonathan Cross, who would begin duties as Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School as of July 18, 2012; Yes 4, No 0, absent Fleming, Philippart, Schmidt. Resolution 12-079, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Ms. Underwood, approved new hires Ashley Conrad, Jaclyn Deatherage, Brigette Garner, Douglas Harrington, and Joseph Shamanski; Yes 4, No 0, same absences. There were no recognition, additions and deletions, public communication, consent agenda, curriculum, business or other items. The meeting was adjourned at 5:35 p.m.; minutes submitted by Todd Miletti, Secretary.

**Consent agenda item B - minutes of August 14, 2012 regular meeting.** President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. immediately following a Special Board Workshop, with Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, along with Superintendent Fowler; administrators Keeling, Lesser, Machesky, Miller, Mull, Rajter and Witt; and approximately 8 additional members of the audience. Resolution 12-080 approved consent items A (minutes of the July 10, 2012, meeting) and B (Treasurer's Report for June and July 2012), 7-0. Resolution 12-081 approved personnel recommendations including new hires Kerry Brennan, Cheryl Buxton, Amy Dent, Ryan Irla, Jessica Jarrard, Matthew Mooney, Lisa Nirganakis, William Ris, Chris Schoonover, and Amy Schwarb, 7-0. Resolution 12-082, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Ms. Underwood, exercised the option permitted by Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 to accept Schools of Choice applications for 2013-2014 for an unlimited number of 9th grade students attending a district in another county whose Intermediate School District is contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, for the purpose of attending the International Academy East program located in the Troy School District; 7-0.

Mrs. Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, presented on Michigan's waiver of No Child Left Behind requirements, filed the prior spring and approved July 19, 2012, and on the Michigan Department of Education labels of Priority, Focus, Reward and Continuous Improvement Schools, explaining the State's focus on the gap between a school's top 30% of highest performing students and bottom 30% of lowest performing students. Mark Rajter presented on the selection of an architectural and engineering firm to assess district facilities and determine scope of work for a potential November 2013 bond issue election; TMP Architecture, Inc. was selected, evaluation would run August 15th to October 9th, and results would come to the Board at the October 16th study session. Asked the approximate cost of the proposed services, Ms. Sara Konieczka stated it was approximately $14,000.

In public communications, Cindy Shankin, teacher at Boulan Park Middle School, described the annual teacher purchase of backpacks filled with school supplies for students from low-income families and showed a sample backpack. Resolution 12-083 cast the Board's ballot for Keith Warnick, Region 8, three-year term, in the 2012 Michigan Association of School Boards Board of Directors election, 7-0. Resolution 12-084 sought monetary aid from the Michigan Association of School Boards Legal Trust Fund (MASB-LTF) to defray legal costs before the Michigan Employment Relations Commission (MERC), where the District was named Respondent in an Unfair Labor Practice charge filed by the Troy Education Association MEA/NEA (TEA) over adoption of a policy relating to the placement of teachers during the term of the collective bargaining agreement set to expire June 30, 2013; the resolution cites sole authority over prohibited subjects of bargaining under Section 15 of the Public Employment Relations Act, MCL 423.215, including new prohibited subjects effective July 2011, and authorized the Superintendent, with assistance from Clark Hill, PLC, to submit the application; 7-0. Resolution 12-085 moved the Board into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(h), for an attorney-client privilege item, on a roll call recorded as Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti, Philippart and Underwood all voting Yes, carried 7-0. The Board moved to closed session at 8:16 p.m., reconvened at 8:20 p.m., and adjourned at 8:49 p.m.

**Consent agenda item C - Bid Award #9745, Adobe.** An August 21, 2012, memorandum from Sara L. Konieczka, Purchasing Supervisor (Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4027, fax 248-823-4077), to Mark S. Rajter reports that bids for Adobe licenses were opened August 16, 2012. Bids were sent to five potential bidders and received from five vendors, none of which was a no bid; two were disqualified for not meeting bid specifications. Packets were reviewed by Merri Lynn Colligan, Director of Technology, and Konieczka. Qualified bids: CDW Government LLC, unit cost $54.24, annual cost $32,815.20, three-year term $98,445.60; Computer Intelligence Association, $52.22, $31,593.10, $94,779.93; Logisoft Computer Products LLC, $51.86, $31,266.40, $93,799.20. The award was recommended to Logisoft Computer Products LLC at $31,266.40 per year for a 3 year term totaling $93,799.20, as an annual expenditure of the General Fund technology budget through fiscal year 2014-15.

**Personnel 6.A - new hires.** Probationary contracts were recommended for the 2012-2013 school year for Kristen Barry (First Grade, Costello Elementary), Ransom Brown (1.0 FTE Physics, Troy High), Sara Carrico (.74 FTE Resource Room, Leonard Elementary/Baker Middle), Melissa Dodge (.6 FTE English, Boulan Park Middle), Talia Dolgin (.5 FTE Speech Pathologist, Services Building), Sharon Douglas-Chong (1.0 FTE Mathematics, Troy High), Giovanna Genovese (Fourth Grade, Hamilton Elementary), Andrea Hinman (.7 FTE Visual Art, Wattles Elementary), Melissa Kijek (.5 FTE Visual Art, Athens High), Theresa Martin (.5 FTE Biology, Troy High), Grayson McKinney (Fourth Grade, Costello Elementary), Michael Messina (1.0 Math, Troy High/Larson Middle), Michael Millman (1.0 FTE EI Classroom, Martell Elementary), Sarah Mockeridge (Kindergarten, Morse Elementary), Ann O'Neill (.5 FTE Counselor, International Academy East), Suzanne Powell (1.0 FTE Counselor, Baker/Larson Middle), Joseph Schmidt (.85 FTE Social Studies/Technology, Baker Middle), Richard Swift (1.0 FTE Resource Room, Troy High), Correen Weber (1.0 FTE Music, Leonard/Hamilton Elementary), and Caitlin Wettlaufer (1.0 FTE Visual Art, Athens High; biographical sketch lists Schroeder/Morse Elementary). Biographical sketches list degrees from Michigan State, Eastern Michigan, Central Michigan, Oakland, Western Michigan, Albion College, the University of Michigan, Northwestern, Columbia University and its Teacher's College, the State University of New York, and Jones International University, with prior service in Detroit, Berkley, Birmingham, Warren Consolidated, Chippewa Valley, Walled Lake, Clarkston, South Lake, East Detroit, Bradford Academy, Riverside Academy, Skokie School District 69, Chicago Public Schools, and Adams 12 School District in Thornton, Colorado.

**Personnel 6.B - staffing update.** Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources, cited drivers of hiring as teacher retirements and resignations tied to MPSERS reforms, the move to full-day kindergarten for 2012/2013, full-year leaves of absence, teacher reduction in FTE status, and increased student enrollment at some buildings. Totals reported: 46 new TSD teachers, 9 teachers previously tenured in another Michigan school district, and 21 teachers with a minimum of a master's degree. New teacher training covers technology, special education matters, diversity and inclusion, curriculum, instruction and assessment, the T.E.A.M. teacher evaluation process, and human resources matters. Under new Board Policy #G-1006 Teacher Placement, adopted June 2012, involuntary transfers were described as minimal: 5 instances raised by the union to date (1 elementary, 4 secondary), of which 2 involved tentative assignments adjusted and 2 were moves consistent with the current contract. In 1 instance at Troy High School a teacher moved from an all-English assignment to an English/Business assignment totaling 3 half-year Business courses; the stated rationale was that the teacher is a Business major and English minor who most recently taught Business courses in 2010/11, while the next English teacher with Business certification had not taught a Business course in 20 years and would have 4 class preps if assigned one.

**Curriculum 7.A - summer learning.** Mike Jolly, Director of Athletics and Enrichment, reviewed summer 2012 programs with Jan Keeling, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Education and Rich Machesky, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Education. Elementary offerings were Nature's ART, Art Master's Mix, Adventures in Learning, Jump Start, GRASP, Title I and ESL (K-7); highlights included a new Adventures in Learning location at Bemis with rotated curriculum and a two-week format, Jump Start expansion with new sites at Costello and Bemis and an additional week, and Title 1 and ESL participation of 90% with 82% of students staying the entire length of the program. Middle school offerings were Academic Adventure Courses, Academic Success Courses, and the Summer Success Academy, in their second year of operation. High school offerings were High School Summer School, Virtual High School Summer School (95% completion rate) and High School ESL, with Intro to PE, Health and World History drawing the largest enrollments. Adult ESL/Youth Services covered Adult ESL, Summer Sensation Camps and Preschool (TOTS). Enrollment, 2012 versus 2011: Elementary Summer Learning (TCE) 291 and 284; Title 1 191 and 165, with Morse 74, Wattles 75 and Costello 42; ESL Title III (K-7 at Morse and Troy Union) 206 and 208; GRASP (Books) 775 and 675; Middle School Summer Learning (TCE) 216 and 202; Summer Success 54 and 49; High School Summer School (TCE) 896 and 881; ESL (Grant Funded) 36 and 52; Adult ESL 169 and 146; Preschool (TOTS) 22 and 29; Summer Sensation Camps 259 and 252.

**Curriculum 7.B - Superintendent's Annual Report 2011-2012.** Although no longer required by the State, the report was shared with the Board. It restates the district purpose of ensuring learning for all members of the school community and the goal that all TSD students be on track to be college and career ready in Literacy, Mathematics, Science and Social Studies, and notes that new College Readiness Cut Scores were implemented for the Fall 2011 MEAP. Graduation rate was 98% for the Class of 2011 and 98% for the Class of 2012, with 95% and 95% attending college. Figures reported for Advanced Placement in 2011-2012 include 1,224 students enrolled, 31% of the student body, and 70% earning college credit; dual enrollment students numbered 32 in 2010-2011 and 51 in 2011-2012. Parent attendance at fall conferences in 2010-11 and 2011-12 was 99% and 99% at elementary, 78% and 86% at middle, and 86% and 85% at high school. Staff measures: 100% of TSD teachers are highly qualified, 57% hold a master's degree or higher, and 8 teachers have earned a Ph.D. or Ed.D. All TSD schools made AYP and all received A grades under the Education YES! Report Card system except Athens High School (B), Baker Middle School (C), Morse Elementary School (B), Niles Community High School (no grade), Smith Middle School (B), and Troy High School (B). Four schools were named Reward Schools - Costello, Hill, Schroeder and Wass Elementary Schools - and twelve were named Focus Schools: Athens High School, Baker Middle School, Barnard Elementary, Bemis Elementary, Boulan Park Middle School, Hamilton Elementary, Larson Middle School, Leonard Elementary, Morse Elementary, Smith Middle School, Troy Union Elementary and Wattles Elementary. All TSD schools are NCA accredited. More than 600 students and staff earned first in state or national honors, there were 52 National Merit Scholar semifinalists, the Class of 2012 earned more than $12 million in scholarships, Troy High, Athens High and IAE ranked in the top 5% of high schools nationwide, and the district had the largest number of Midwest Talent Search winners in the state. First-place state finishes included the Michigan Chess Championships, Science Olympiad, Michigan Fed Challenge, DECA, American Mathematics Competition, Michigan China Quiz Bowl, the Michigan Annual Japanese Speech Contest, and the Michigan Interscholastic Press Association Competition; national placements included perfect ACT/Explorer scores, the Siemens Challenge/Intel Science Fair, National Ocean Science Bowl, Robofest National Competition, National MathCounts, Future Problem Solver International Competition, and the NASA-sponsored International YouTube Space Lab Competition. Board honors included the MASB President's Award, being 1 of 8 to earn the Visionary Leadership Award, 1 of 11 Michigan boards to earn the Standard of Excellence Award, 2 Board members receiving the Presidential Award as the highest level of certification, and multiple members certified beyond Level 1. Full district and individual building reports with cover letters are posted at www.troy.k12.mi.us and on every school homepage.

**Curriculum 7.C - enrollment update.** Jan Keeling and Dr. Rich Machesky presented counts reported that morning, comparing September 6, 2011 with September 4, 2012. Elementary: Barnard 512 and 508; Bemis 519 and 532; Costello 369 and 354; Hamilton 439 and 470; Hill 332 and 319; Leonard 435 and 437; Martell 401 and 422; Morse 450 and 454; Schroeder 516 and 536; Troy Union 440 and 455; Wass 393 and 411; Wattles 463 and 472; Early Childhood 37 and 29; elementary total 5,306 and 5,399. Middle schools: Baker 738 and 698; Boulan 719 and 709; Larson 705 and 718; Smith 725 and 672; total 2,887 and 2,797. High schools: Athens 1,594 and 1,612; Troy 1,971 and 2,012; IAE 442 and 457; NCHS 154 and 133; GROW 31 and 35; total 4,192 and 4,249. Total students 12,385 and 12,445.

**Curriculum 7.D and Other.** Kerry Birmingham, Director of Community and Media Relations, reported on the official launch of the new Troy School District websites the prior week, designed by webmasters from 19 schools and the District who migrated content from the old sites. Under Other, a suggested resolution would reschedule the November 6, 2012, Board of Education meeting to November 13, 2012, at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building.
